name: Thomas DiArgo
caption: Won the first match the federation ever staged, pinning "Silky Smooth" Ricky Perez with the D-Drop after a ring speech declaring himself its future World Heavyweight Champion.

tenures.source: The promotion's own first broadcast, 7 January 2001.

name: Ricky Perez
caption: Lost the federation's first match to Thomas DiArgo after his Suave Sault found only the mat.

tenures.source: The promotion's own first broadcast, 7 January 2001.

name: "Texas" Jack Williams
caption: Debuted on the first broadcast and beat a surprise replacement opponent, Mark Destructo, with the Long Neck Bottle, a neckbreaker from the top rope.

tenures.source: The promotion's own first broadcast, 7 January 2001.

name: Mark Destructo
caption: Appeared unannounced as a replacement opponent on the first broadcast and lost to "Texas" Jack Williams after three chair shots and the Long Neck Bottle.

tenures.source: The promotion's own first broadcast, 7 January 2001.

identity.note: A Marc Destructo is ranked in the newsgroup's 1996 poll under another federation's tag; the spelling differs, five years separate the two, and no document ties them together, so the records stay apart.

name: The Renaissance Man
caption: A seven-foot-four returning wrestler who pinned Doug Fury with the Shattered Dream in the first main event, six months after Fury had broken his ribs.

tenures.source: The promotion's own first broadcast, 7 January 2001.

identity.note: A same-named wrestler is on record in a 2004 federation; three years separate the two and no document ties them together, so the records stay apart.

name: Doug Fury
caption: Lost the first main event to the Renaissance Man after the arrival of "Outlaw" Joe Wayans stopped him cold, and closed the night in a stare-down with Wayans.

tenures.source: The promotion's own first broadcast, 7 January 2001.

name: Joe Wayans
caption: Walked out during the first main event to a deafening reaction, distracting Doug Fury into the loss, and ended the broadcast staring him down.

tenures.source: The promotion's own first broadcast, 7 January 2001.

name: Brian Knight
caption: The front-office figure who opened the first broadcast, declared the federation born, and promised a Royal Rumble the following week to crown its first Heavyweight Champion.

tenures.source: The promotion's own first broadcast, 7 January 2001.

identity.note: A same-named wrestler billed as a former world champion is on record in a 1997 federation, and this one is described as a many-time world champion; four years separate the two and no document names both runs, so the records stay apart pending a primary source.

name: Bryan Broon
caption: Called the first broadcast at the announce table beside Mark Travis, signing off under the spelling Brian Broon.

tenures.source: The promotion's own first broadcast, 7 January 2001.

name: Mark Travis
caption: Called the first broadcast at the announce table beside Bryan Broon, cheering on Doug Fury throughout the main event.

tenures.source: The promotion's own first broadcast, 7 January 2001.
